newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Baloise gets Italian okay to sell units.
newsitem.headline: Baloise gets Italian okay to sell units.

text.p: Swiss insurer Baloise said Italian authorities had approved the sale of two subsidiaries in northern Italy to Banca Carige, a deal announced in May.
The sale affects Baloise subsidiary Norditalia, including its unit Basilese Vita Nuova, and Levante.
"The sale of the companies is now complete and operational responsibility has been transferred to the new owner," Baloise said in a statement.
"We are receiving 150 billion lira ($81.6 million) for the sale," a Baloise spokesman said.
Under terms of the sale, Baloise will retain a 10-percent stake in all three of its former Italian subsidiaries.
It will also take a stake in Carige of around four percent.
Genoa-based Carige already held 20 percent of Levante and Basilese Vita Nova before this deal and is now buying the remainder except for the Baloise minority holdings.
The sale follows similar moves by Baloise to exit France, Spain and Italy and concentrate on more profitable markets in Switzerland, Germany, Belgium, Luxembourg and Austria.
The geographic realignment was announced last December,
Baloise offers life and non-life direct insurance. It posted net profit last year of 191.4 million Swsis francs against 161.1 million in 1995. -- Zurich Newsroom, +41-1-631 7340
